subject: CorePulse - probe visibility mismatch & maintenance offset credit request
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@corepulse.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: support@corepulse.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Repeated partial degradations 2027-03-15 — request for credit

Hi Neha,

We saw repeated 500-level spikes and elevated p95 latency from 04:10–04:40 UTC on 2027-03-15 that impacted our API calls routed to the us-west region. Our telemetry shows failed requests correlating with your public status page entry and a maintenance note, but CorePulse probes show a longer window of impact than your maintenance window.

We attached our aggregated logs and request traces. Per our SLA we’re requesting a credit for the affected window; we’d like Redwood to confirm how you calculated the uptime window and whether third-party DB maintenance (which you listed under "dependent services") should attenuate the credit.

Next steps: please confirm the exact event windows from Redwood probes, what third-party exclusions were applied, and a proposed credit amount.

Thanks,
Aisha
VP, Platform Engineering
CorePulse Systems

Attachments: corepulse_downtime_log_20270315.csv
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@corepulse.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated partial degradations 2027-03-15 — request for credit

Hi Aisha — thanks for the quick note and the logs. We’re investigating and I’ve looped in Marissa and Karthik to help with SLA accounting & routing traces. Initial answers:

- We show an operational maintenance window at 04:15–04:25 UTC for a rolling config push on the inference edge that affected a subset of nodes.
- A downstream DB provider reported a maintenance that overlapped but started earlier (04:08 UTC) and had some instability after the DB window completed.
- Our probe network and CorePulse’s probes have different fanouts; that can cause apparent window differences.

We’ll reconcile logs and send a consolidated timeline with probe traces attached. Can you confirm whether the attached CSV includes request IDs so we can crosswalk exact transactions?

Neha
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Aisha Rahman <aisha@corepulse.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 13:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated partial degradations 2027-03-15 — request for credit

Quick update from SRE side and preliminary reconciliation attached (redwood_probe_traces_region-west-20270315.zip). Key points:

- Our continuous probes observed error elevation across three clusters in us-west between 04:12–04:36 UTC (regional aggregation). The config push produced a rolling restart pattern causing transient KV-cache warm-up that increased p95 for a subset of routes.
- The DB maintenance created tail errors that extended error rates for queries against that shard until ~04:42 UTC.
- Per our SLA, third-party maintenance is generally considered for exclusion if the downstream provider is explicitly listed and the failure is isolated to that dependency. In this case the pattern shows both an internal rolling config impact and downstream DB instability.

Proposal: apportion the affected window into two slices — 04:12–04:25 UTC attributed to Redwood rolling change (eligible for credit), and 04:25–04:42 UTC considered downstream impact (partial exclusion). We propose a credit reflecting the portion attributable to Redwood.

I’m adding Jonas to review probe sampling and ensure the apportionment math is sound.

—Marissa
Director, Reliability Engineering
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@corepulse.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated partial degradations 2027-03-15 — request for credit

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the initial apportionment. A few clarifying points from our compliance team:

- CorePulse’s traffic is multi-homed and we saw impacted latency from two distinct POPs (us-west-2a and us-west-2b). Both showed degradation for nearly the full 04:10–04:42 UTC range.
- Our legal/compliance team asks that Redwood include probe sampling variance in the reconciliation (i.e., how many probes saw the issue simultaneously, not just regional aggregates).
- We also need the signed results of any downstream vendor maintenance tickets you relied on for exclusion.

Can you provide:
1) per-pop probe counts and raw trace IDs for crosswalk
2) the vendor maintenance ticket ID or DocuSign-equivalent evidence
3) a concrete credit calculation and invoice offset amount so we can route internally

Best,
Aisha
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@corepulse.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated partial degradations 2027-03-15 — request for credit

Aisha — attaching per-pop probe extraction (see related_links). Summary of technical reconciliation:

- Probe visibility: 12 active Redwood probes targeted at the us-west region; 9 of 12 observed >1% error elevation between 04:12–04:26 UTC. All 12 observed elevated error rates between 04:26–04:36 UTC, matching CorePulse’s extended window.
- Crosswalk: we matched 3,212 CorePulse request IDs to Redwood ingress logs; ~72% of the failed requests during 04:12–04:25 map to nodes that had rolling restarts.
- Vendor evidence: downstream DB provider ticket #DB-7723 (public excerpt attached via secure drive link) shows maintenance at 04:08–04:20 with residual retries until ~04:42.

Credit calculation (proposed): apportion impacted time 14 minutes attributable to Redwood (04:12–04:26) out of total 32-minute impact window (04:10–04:42) — proposed invoice credit = (14/32) * monthly uptime creditable fraction for that billing period. In dollars: $3,480 credit (detailed calc attached).

If CorePulse accepts, Neha can start the credit process and we’ll include vendor ticket references in the audit bundle. If you disagree with apportionment we can schedule a 30-min technical sync.

-Jonas
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@corepulse.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated partial degradations 2027-03-15 — request for credit

Thanks for the detailed reconciliation and calculations. We accept the apportionment methodology but request the following before formal agreement:

1) redacted copy of DB-7723 (we only need timestamps and confirmation of affected shard IDs)
2) a short one-page note from Redwood SRE confirming the rolling config change timeline and list of affected node IDs for audit purposes
3) a formal credit notice with invoice offset line item we can attach to our accounts payable request

If those items are supplied by EOD tomorrow we’ll process the credit on our side. Otherwise we’ll need a short technical call Friday morning.

Appreciate the collaborative work here.

—Aisha
